steps.title: Build initial PubMed query
steps.instruction: Open PubMed Advanced Search (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/advanced/), add "Sudan" in the Affiliation field, set Date Publication from "2003/01/01" to "present" (or use "3000" as the upper bound), combine with AND, and click “add to history”. The resulting query is ((Sudan[Affiliation]) AND (("2003/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "3000"[Date - Publication])))

steps.title: Add bioinformatics terms to query
steps.instruction: For each term – “Next generation sequencing”, “Genomics”, “Bioinformatics”, “Sequencing”, “Computational Biology”, “in silico” – select the All Fields box, type the term, and click “add to history” (or search directly). This creates separate queries each combined with the base Sudan query as shown above.

steps.title: Export PubMed results to RIS
steps.instruction: For each query, open the results page, sort by “Best match”, click “send to citation manager”, choose “All results”, create a RIS file, and save it to a designated repository.

steps.title: Search ScienceDirect with same terms
steps.instruction: Go to ScienceDirect Advanced Search (https://www.sciencedirect.com/search), repeat the affiliation and date settings, add the same bioinformatics terms one by one, sort by “Best match”, and export the citations (e.g., RIS) to the repository.

steps.title: Import citations into EndNote
steps.instruction: Open EndNote version x9.3.3 (Build 13966) and create a library named "Bioinfromatics_in_Sudan_All_Search_terms.enl". Import all RIS files obtained from PubMed and ScienceDirect into this library.

steps.title: Create custom EndNote style
steps.instruction: In EndNote, open “Reference Types” and select “Journal Article”. Then choose “Insert Field” and add fields in this order, separated by tabs: Year, Title, Author, Journal, Volume, Issue, DOI. Exit and save the style as "Bioinfromatics_in_Sudan_All_Search_terms_excel".

substeps.instruction: Open Reference Types → select Journal Article
Insert Field → Year ⟶ Tab ⟶ Title ⟶ Tab ⟶ Author ⟶ Tab ⟶ Journal ⟶ Tab ⟶ Volume ⟶ Tab ⟶ Issue ⟶ Tab ⟶ DOI

steps.title: Export references as text file
steps.instruction: Make a copy of the original EndNote library "Bioinfromatics_in_Sudan_All_Search_terms.enl", then choose “Export References”, select the previously created style, and save the output as a plain‑text file (*.txt).

steps.title: Import text into Excel
steps.instruction: Open a blank Excel workbook, go to File → Open, select the exported *.txt file, and in the Text Import Wizard choose “Delimited”, leave all other options at their defaults, then click Next and Finish to load the data into the sheet.

substeps.instruction: Text Import Wizard: Delimited, default settings

steps.title: Replace carriage returns with semicolons
steps.instruction: In Excel, open Edit → Find and Replace, set “Find what” to the special carriage‑return character, set “Replace with” to "; " (semicolon and space), choose “Any field”, click Search, then Replace All.

steps.title: Remove duplicate records
steps.instruction: Use EndNote’s Find Duplicates function to locate and delete duplicate entries; manually review any remaining duplicates that EndNote missed (e.g., different journal name formats).

steps.title: Apply inclusion criteria
steps.instruction: Keep only articles that are written in English, have at least one author affiliated with a Sudanese institution (affiliation field contains "Sudan"), and incorporate bioinformatics techniques as defined by Luscombe et al. 2001 (Methods of Information in Medicine 2001;40(04):346‑58).

steps.title: Apply exclusion criteria
steps.instruction: Discard any article that: (a) is affiliated with South Sudan (post‑2011), (b) is available only as an abstract (no full‑text confirmation of bioinformatics tool use), or (c) is a review paper (40 identified) lacking a bioinformatics tool application.

steps.title: Order articles by year and count
steps.instruction: Sort the filtered Excel list by the Year column, count the number of articles per year, and record these frequencies in a separate sheet to generate a yearly publication figure.

steps.title: Categorize articles by research area
steps.instruction: Using each article’s title, keywords, and journal scope, assign it to a research area, tally the number of articles per area, and list the counts in Excel for a research‑area distribution figure.

steps.title: Save final dataset for analysis
steps.instruction: Save the completed Excel workbook (including filtered records, yearly counts, and research‑area counts) as the final dataset to be used for downstream data analysis.
